title: September 11, 2001
subject: histoire
description: On **September 11, 2001**, nineteen Al-Qaeda terrorists hijack four planes. The deadliest attack in American history ushers in the era of the war on terrorism.

hero.hook: A September morning that closes the post-Cold War era and opens a century of wars.

blocks.text: On Tuesday **September 11, 2001**, nineteen members of , a terrorist organization founded by **Osama Bin Laden**, hijacked four planes. Two hit the **World Trade Center** in New York, a third the **Pentagon**, headquarters of the American defense. The fourth crashed in Pennsylvania after the passengers' revolt. **[[Al-Qaeda]]**
Results: **2 977** dead. Beyond the drama, the attack ends the hope of a peaceful world order and triggers a series of conflicts which are still shaping the 21st century.

blocks.text: The signs are piling up: attack on the World Trade Center in **1993**, East African embassies in **1998**, destroyer USS Cole in **2000**. However, the compartmentalization between the CIA and the FBI, American intelligence services, prevents the wires from being connected in time.
The 19 hijackers spent approximately **400,000** dollars on an attack whose overall economic cost will exceed **2 trillion**.

At **8:46 a.m.**, American Flight 11 hits the North Tower. At **9:03**, United 175 hits the South Tower live on TV. At **9:37**, American 77 hits the Pentagon. At **10:03**, United 93 crashes in Pennsylvania.

blocks.caption: The Twin Towers of the World Trade Center, central targets of the attacks.

blocks.text: The towers collapse: South at **9:59 a.m.**, North at **10:28 a.m.**. American airspace is closed for the first time. These images become the founding trauma of a generation.

In October **2001**, operation aimed at Afghanistan: destroy Al-Qaeda and overthrow the **[[Enduring Freedom]]**, the Islamist movement which sheltered Bin Laden. Kabul falls quickly. The war lasts twenty years. **[[Taliban]]**

In March **2003**, without a UN mandate, the United States launched , accusing the dictator  of weapons of mass destruction. The accusation is false; the country falls into chaos. At , an American base in Cuba, detainees remain outside of traditional law. Bin Laden was killed on **May 1, 2011** in Pakistan. **[[Saddam Hussein]]** **[[Guantanamo]]** [[The Iraq War (2003)]]

In the United States, the **PATRIOT Act**, an emergency law, massively expands surveillance. Europe follows. Airports are forever changing. Ground Zero, site of the collapsed towers, becomes a memorial and symbol of resilience.
The wars that followed caused hundreds of thousands of deaths and millions of displaced people. Global terrorism, more decentralized, uses the tools of globalization to combat it.
**September 11, 2001** transforms a threat into a global war: interventions in Afghanistan and Iraq, and a lasting security shift in democracies.
